overall_summary: Deduplication reveals 47 unique shorts. First-person what-if cosmic immersion and extreme exoplanet environments dominate channel metrics (averaging 700-1,000+ views with healthy 3.5%+ like ratios), particularly videos around 19-21 seconds. Conversely, repeated uploads and dry psychology/brain facts ('fake memories', 'songs stuck in head') consistently stagnate below 100 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Extreme Cosmic Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) far outperform standard fact recitations.
winning_patterns.action: Use visceral 2nd-person sensory framing ('What If You Stepped Onto...') targeting extreme celestial bodies, keeping duration at 20-21s.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,030 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) hit the highest baseline audience engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Focus hooks on counter-intuitive, cinematic planetary extremes rather than generic space trivia.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' across three uploads generated only 5, 10, and 53 views; brain/song loops averaged <40 views.
weak_patterns.action: Retire generic psychology and memory trivia; avoid re-uploading identical scripts under the same title.

weak_patterns.evidence: 12-15s clips like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (118-183 views) and 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' repeat uploads saw severe flatlining.
weak_patterns.action: Eliminate low-effort 12-15s static trivia in favor of narrative-driven 19-21s cinematic micro-journeys.
